name: FourBoxOceanHeatUptake
description:
This example component splits a global effective radiative forcing into heat uptake
in each region of the four-box grid.
It shows how a component reads a scalar input and writes a four-box output.

# Physics

Ocean heat uptake varies by region because of:

- Ocean and land: oceans have a higher heat capacity and absorb more energy
- Latitude: polar regions take up heat differently
- Mixing: deep ocean mixing affects how far heat penetrates

The component scales the forcing by a fixed ratio for each region.
The four ratios must average to 1, so the area-weighted mean uptake equals the global forcing.

# Example

```rust
use rscm_components::{
    FourBoxOceanHeatUptake,
    FourBoxOceanHeatUptakeParameters,
};

let params = FourBoxOceanHeatUptakeParameters::default();
let component = FourBoxOceanHeatUptake::from_parameters(params);
```

parameters.name: northern_ocean_ratio
parameters.description: Ratio of northern ocean heat uptake to the global effective radiative forcing

parameters.name: northern_land_ratio
parameters.description: Ratio of northern land heat uptake to the global effective radiative forcing

parameters.name: southern_ocean_ratio
parameters.description: Ratio of southern ocean heat uptake to the global effective radiative forcing

parameters.name: southern_land_ratio
parameters.description: Ratio of southern land heat uptake to the global effective radiative forcing
